checks.finding: The existing outer FLASH write/readback remains before both calls. The new method independently reads FLASH.CR2.WAIT and requires the caller-supplied expected maximum, returning FlashLatencyTimeout otherwise. Callers supply the unchanged family MAX_FLASH_WAIT, 1 for L010 and 3 for L011/L012; no expected value is inferred from current hardware.

Cr2(self.routes) constructs a local value from the original frozen word. set_flashwait changes only its typed FLASHWAIT field. The actual complete current SYSCTRL.CR2 must equal that expected word. The own input descriptions place FLASHWAIT at 6:4 and FLASH WAIT at 2:0 for all three families. The method neither writes the hardware mirror nor masks WAIT out of native start.

Full-word equality against the original word with only FLASHWAIT replaced retains comparison of all non-WAIT bits, including brake routes, wake/debug/lockup controls, reserved bits and L010 RTCLPM. Unexpected mirror WAIT also rejects.
IER and LSE are compared as complete words against the original Admission. No fresh current-word snapshot replaces either original field.

The original native preflight still rejects an unqualified monitor before it can return an Admission. The new operation uses the original Option<LSI TRIM, WAIT> and repeats current monitor_qualified plus tuple equality. L010 keeps its inherited stable legal-LSI policy; L011/L012 keep their own valid-factory checks, own address and typed TRIM masking. It does not run preflight again or let later LSI readiness manufacture an original admission. Stability is checked at the existing/new observation points; no continuous hardware-stability measurement is claimed.

The returned Self changes only routes; struct update carries reused, lsi, lse and interrupts verbatim. Original fresh/reused branching remains in native start. MONITOR_LSI conflict checking and its only start-time assignment remain there, unchanged.

The added call is inside the existing Some(config.lse)/Some(admission) block and runs only when lse_target.is_none(). Existing LSE-target admission refresh, original snapshot checks, first-LSI-request classification, target finish path and ownership policies retain all original bytes. HSI/HSE auxiliary paths gain only the approved read-only rebase before the unchanged start call.

The single added line rebases the original Admission immediately before native start inside the existing Some/Some block. Both current public targets remain HSI/HSE. No L012 LSE SYSCLK option or new feature is introduced.
Config.lse=None cannot enter either existing conditional. It gains no new snapshot, register read, source request, gate operation or eligibility condition.

Native start is byte-preserved after a line-number shift. Its first full CR2/IER/LSE guard, monitor qualification/conflict checks, original fresh/reused branch, central checks, configuration consumers, pad ownership, L011/L012 commit-edge full-word checks, final CR2/IER guard and fault/readiness handling are unchanged.

The new operation contains reads, local typed-value mutation and a returned copied Admission only. Its called qualification/parameter helpers are unchanged readers. It performs no MMIO write, peripheral gate/reset operation, oscillator request, GPIO operation, preflight recapture or MONITOR_LSI assignment. FLASH is already enabled by the unchanged outer transition.

The added guard runs at the existing start edge after the existing partial clock transition. No rollback, gate restoration, ownership or publication policy changes. On its rejection, no new source/pad/gate write has occurred. On an admitted owned-WAIT change, the previously blocked path may intentionally proceed to existing native startup and later clock writes. This is not a claim that the complete successful path has no effects.

Existing WAIT-only hardware writes retain their original bytes. L012 FETCH/CACHE/CACHEINVALID and reserved fields are not changed by this correction; L010/L011 reserved FLASH fields retain their existing treatment.

error_contract.wrong_authoritative_flash_wait: FlashLatencyTimeout before returning an adjusted Admission. This is an explicit added guard, so error priority is not claimed globally identical to the baseline.
error_contract.wrong_sysctrl_mirror_or_non_wait_cr2_or_: LseClockInUse; original snapshot values are not overwritten to hide the change.
error_contract.following_native_start_errors: Unchanged existing guard/consumer/pad/readiness behavior after the read-only rebase succeeds.
error_contract.gate_side_effects: No new gate operations or restoration behavior; existing pre-call partial transition and permanent software pad reservations remain.

state_reasoning.method: Independent static path analysis, not executed test cases.
state_reasoning.already_maximum_wait: The expected full word equals the original full word; the method cannot remove unrelated differences.
state_reasoning.invalid_incoming_wait: Existing above-maximum rejection before the owned write is unchanged.
modes_reviewed: unchanged existing L010/L011 LSE SYSCLK branch
state_reasoning.interpretation: These are code-path conclusions under documented source semantics and existing exclusive-init entry requirements, not runtime pass results.
